subject: Information Theory
title: Error Correction in 5G
description: A micro-lesson that makes Error Correction in 5G usable.

hook.text: 5G promises gigabit speeds over radio waves bouncing off buildings. Error correction makes that wild claim real.

buildup.text: Radio channels are harsh: multipath fading, interference, and mobility cause unpredictable error patterns.

discovery.text: 5G NR uses LDPC codes for data channels and polar codes for control channels. Both approach Shannon's limit.

twist.text: Adaptive modulation and coding adjust the code rate in real time. Good signal? Less protection, more speed.

climax.text: The combination of near-capacity codes and adaptive rates lets 5G deliver reliable gigabit speeds in messy environments.

punchline.text: Bouncing signals, moving phones. Codes keep data intact.

quiz.question: Which two code families does 5G NR use?
options: LDPC for data and polar codes for control
